title: How I tested a coal train’s first delivery in Godot
author: ventayol
selftext:
I built a playable preview of Fourways, an OpenTTD-inspired transport tycoon, in one week with Claude and Codex. I started from scratch and worked on it in my spare time alongside my full-time job.



I used Claude to help build a playtest that runs through the first coal route in Godot. It drives the game’s UI to lay track, build stations, and buy a steam train. Then it checks that the train follows its orders, delivers the coal, and earns money. I can rerun it on the same map seed as I change the game.



That first payout gives me a concrete check that construction, train orders, cargo delivery, and the economy still work together. The playtest also captures frames along the way, which I used for the gameplay clips.



If you’re building a simulation with coding agents, how do you test the parts that only make sense once they’re running together? I’m happy to answer questions about my process.
